subject: Intermittent reachability to on-prem services after private backplane cutover
messages:
From: Alice Jansen <alice.jansen@quillon.co>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent reachability to on-prem services after private backplane cutover

Hi Karthik,

We started a backplane cutover last night to migrate our private VPC connectivity to Redwood's hybrid backplane. Since the cutover completed (approx 02:30 UTC) we've observed intermittent failures from Redwood-hosted callers to a subset of our on-prem API endpoints (10.20.11.0/24). Symptoms: successful requests ~85% of the time, but 15% of requests time out or see TCP RSTs mid-session; bulk transfers occasionally fail with retransmits.

Attached traceroute and a short pcap from one failing attempt (edge-capture-20270601.pcap). Key observations from our side:
- Failures appear correlated to larger packets (responses >1200 bytes).
- The path includes an on-prem NAT appliance and a pair of hybrid edge boxes that perform SNAT for hairpinned flows.

Can the Redwood networking team triage? We're seeing customer impact on a small but critical subset of API calls. Happy to hop on a call — we can be available 13:00-17:00 UTC today.

Attachments: cutover-traceroute.txt, edge-capture-20270601.pcap

Thanks,
Alice Jansen
NetOps Lead, Quillon Logistics
alice.jansen@quillon.co

Subject: Re: Intermittent reachability to on-prem services after private backplane cutover

Hi Alice — thanks for the quick signal and for attaching the traceroute/pcap. I'm escalating to our private deployment networking squad (looping Vanessa and Marissa).

First pass questions so we can prioritize:
- Can you confirm whether those on-prem endpoints are behind a stateful NATs appliance that rewrites source ports (you hinted yes)?
- Any recent firewall/security group changes on the on-prem side at the time of cutover?
- Do you have MTU configured on the hybrid edges or are they passing PMTU? (the pcap hints at fragmentation-related retransmits)

Vanessa / Marissa — initial read: traces show a short-lived RST sequence and retransmits where payload size >1200B. My immediate suspects: MTU/fragmentation path issues, asymmetric routing causing replies to take a different edge, or SNAT port exhaustion/hairpin with ephemeral port reuse. Could we triage logs for conntrack/ephemeral port pressure on the edge nodes that handled the failing sessions? I can coordinate a call with Quillon at 13:30 UTC if that helps.

Alice — we'll collect some packet counters and kernel conntrack stats; expect an update in ~2–3 hours.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Alice Jansen <alice.jansen@quillon.co>
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent reachability to on-prem services after private backplane cutover

Thanks for the details and the pcap — I pulled the edge boxes' conntrack and SNAT logs for the timeframe in the pcap. Summary of findings:

- Asymmetric routing: some return traffic from the on-prem NAT is seen back to a different edge node (edge-b) than the one that originated the outbound flow (edge-a). That explains the occasional RSTs (no conntrack entry on the return path).
- Conntrack port churn: edge-a shows a high ephemeral port churn during the cutover window; when flows hairpin through the on-prem NAT we see SNAT port reuse collisions (~0.5% of flows) — correlated with the 15% failure rate Alice reported.
- MTU/fragmentation: a subset of captured responses were fragmented; we saw MSS 1460 on TCP syns but PMTU discovery failing in a couple of exchanges (ICMP unreachable filtered by an intermediate firewall).

Recommended mitigations (short-term / urgent):
1) Apply MSS clamping to 1360 on hybrid edge egress toward on-prem to avoid fragmentation for now. Quick config snippet attached (quick-mitigation-snippet.txt).
2) Temporarily enable sticky routing for Quillon flows (pin flows to originating edge node) to avoid return-path asymmetry while we reconcile backplane route propagation.
3) Increase conntrack_max and ephemeral port range on edges to reduce SNAT port collisions until we roll a config change on the on-prem NAT to use a larger translation pool.

Longer term: A design follow-up to eliminate hairpin SNAT for these subnets (DNAT back to internal host or hairpin bypass) and make PMTU/ICMP handling explicit in the cutover playbook.

I'll schedule a 30-minute mitigation window with Quillon for tomorrow 14:00 UTC. Karthik — can you approve the sticky-route ACL and MSS clamp before I push?

Vanessa Ortiz
Staff Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alice Jansen <alice.jansen@quillon.co>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent reachability to on-prem services after private backplane cutover

Thanks — confirmed for the 2027-06-04 14:00 UTC maintenance window. We've queued the on-prem NAT team and our firewall team to accept the temporary MSS clamp and to expand the NAT translation pool for the change window.

Quick notes from our side after additional captures:
- We saw a marked reduction in retransmits when we forced TLS responses to 1200B during a brief test, which matches Vanessa's MSS hypothesis.
- PCAP IDs for the attached test traces: capture-2417 / capture-2418 (uploaded to the Drive folder you shared).

We'll be standing by during the window and can provide live captures. Appreciate the quick escalation.

Alice Jansen
